paragraph: Ramsey's single-family market is the main event here, with 40 sales over six months at a median of $999,500, essentially right at the million mark. The typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with two full baths, with ranches and split-levels filling in behind it, and closings ran from $470,000 up to $2,450,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Homes are going in about 15 days, 55% closed above asking, and the sale-to-list ratio sits at 1.02. That is a competitive market, and you should expect competition on anything priced right. Single-family closings built from 6 in March to 10 in June and 12 in July, and the July median of $1,250,500 is the strongest of any month with real volume, so there is no sign of the usual late-summer softening yet. Condos and townhouses, by contrast, run 23 sales at a median of $605,000, mostly two-bedroom, two-bath townhouses. That tier is tighter than the houses: 65% sold above asking, a 1.04 ratio, and a 12-day median. Sellers are dictating terms there, and the monthly counts are too thin to read a trend inside it. If you're weighing the two, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a townhouse.
